precepts.text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee. The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. You know which sins you deal with, yet you still entertain them.
precepts.point: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out. We got to repent as a nation, and in the context of this topic, repent from alcoholism. It is not something you can play with; you cannot play with sin.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
“Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out”. We have to repent as a nation, and in the context of this class, repent from alcoholism. You have to stop. It is not something you can play with. You cannot play with sin.

That is why God says, “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee”. It will bite you. You do not stand close to a serpent and see how long you can last; you flee from it.

“The teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” That is sin. It is going into the sins you know you deal with. You know which particular sins you struggle with, and yet you still entertain them.

Deacon Joshua said it: you should be able to go six months. Just drop it for six months. Especially you big brothers: drop the alcohol for six months and watch how fast you get in the green, because every week you take away 4,000 calories. To repent and be converted is to flee from the bottle, not to keep it near and hope it does not bite.

precepts.text: Moses truly said, a prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things. And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people. You reject Christ and what he said, that is your outcome. precepts.point: Touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using; after the commandments and doctrines of men. Stop following man. Christ has come; he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary and his sacrifice is supreme.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me”. Peter is getting this from Deuteronomy 18:15 to 19, and that prophet is Christ.

“him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.” Hear him in how many things? All things. “And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.” You reject Christ, you reject what he said, and that is your outcome.

This is what Paul was warning the Colossians about. The men beguiling them were trying to trick and deceive the followers of Christ into going back to the carnal ordinances of animal sacrifice: get that lamb, get that ram, get that goat, get that ox. Christ taught that his sacrifice is supreme, and every soul that will not hear him on it shall be destroyed from among the people.

precepts.text: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the laws are what convert a man.
precepts.point: What converts us is the law of the Lord, which is perfect, converting the soul.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Peter says, “Repent ye therefore, and be converted”: converted means changed. But what converts us? David answers: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The laws of God are perfect, and they are what convert the soul. So back in Acts 3, when Peter says repent and be converted, what converts us is the laws of God.

That conversion is what makes the rest of the verse possible: “that your sins may be blotted out”, forgotten, washed away, “when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.” The times of refreshing are the times of the kingdom being brought upon the earth, when the earth is refreshed.

Ezekiel shows what repentance means in the Old Testament, read right alongside it: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, saith the Lord God. Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions.” When you repent, you turn away from your transgressions. You turn from sin, and the perfect law of the Lord is what turns you and changes your soul.

God is a God of those that repent, as Manasseh found. He did not call the righteous but sinners to repentance, and the way a sinner is converted is by coming under the law of the Lord.

precepts.text: Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, and in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed. Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities. The blessing on all kindreds of the earth is Christ dying for the Israelites scattered in every nation, whose blood covers us wherever we are found, since we cannot reach all our people on this earth.
precepts.point: The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.” The heathen are the Gentiles: the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, justified through faith. But Christians say, see, brother, all nations will be blessed. So what does it mean?

Peter answers: “Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days.” They foretold, as Paul says the scripture foresaw. “Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers”. The ye are the Israelites. Abraham was a prophet, and the covenant passed from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob, “saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.”

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” Unto you first, the Israelites. The blessing is Christ dying for the Israelites, for all of us scattered among all the nations. The earth is too big for us to reach all our people, but Christ's blood covers us wherever we are found. That is how all the kindreds of the earth are blessed: Israel scattered among those nations and blessed with the death of Christ.

And Esau? He already got his blessing: blood and death, slavery, weaponry, war, bloodshed, nukes and witchcraft. He is literally dropping those blessings on Iran right now. He does not need any more. The other nations' blessing is to work, to build up our kingdom, and to survive the destruction as servants. “So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

precepts.text: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.
precepts.point: Speak truth with your neighbour, let him that stole steal no more, and grieve not the Holy Spirit.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts”. The former conversation is the ways of this world, the love of this world. The old man, or old woman, is corrupt and filthy in the eyesight of the Lord, and that mentality manifests itself all the time. The ways of this world are deceitful lusts, hooks in your spirit that will take your soul out of the game. “And be renewed in the spirit of your mind”: by the scriptures. There must be change. That old man must be killed. If you are still the same three or four years in this truth, brothers and sisters, you need to really examine yourself; something is not right.

Acts shows the difference: “Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out”. First repent: you stop your sin, you stop breaking the laws of God. Then be converted, which is the actions behind that. You have to have a pattern of righteousness to follow, a pattern of good works, not dabbling in your old sin.

You used to lie; you used to steal. You are not doing those any more. But now what are you doing? You are speaking uprightly to your brothers. You are working, because now you need a manner of provision to provide not only for yourself and your family but for your nation that depends on you. That is the converted part: the works that follow repentance, showing that you truly repented and are no longer that old man or that old woman.

So “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” Put on the king that you are, and sisters, the attributes of your foremothers, the daughters of Sarah. Put away lying, “Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour”, and let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth. If you are not investing in the scriptures, the old man will come out in wickedness.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Why are the sacrifices of the set feasts no longer brought? “But those things, which God before had shewed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.”

The prophets showed before that Christ should suffer, and he has so fulfilled it. His suffering did away with the law of animal sacrifice. The feasts of the Lord remain; what Christ fulfilled is the burnt offerings, meat offerings, drink offerings and peace offerings that were tied to them, so what is left for us is the living sacrifice of the body.

The restitution of all things is the kingdom restored to Israel. Heaven must receive Christ until those times, and we are living the restitution of all things right now, before he comes.

precepts.text: Israel would discontinue from the heritage the Most High gave, so the heritage, meaning the identity, land, language, culture, and foods, was lost.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Here is what Israel lost: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

The heritage the Most High gave was lost: the identity, the land, the language, the culture and the foods. Israel would serve their enemies in a land they did not know. That heritage is what has to be restored, and its restoration is the restitution of all things.

precepts.text: "I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men," showing the remembrance of the people was lost.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The remembrance of the people was lost. Scattered into corners, Israel was forgotten among men.

Something lost is something to be restored. The remembrance of who Israel is being brought back is part of the restitution of all things.

precepts.text: The enemies take crafty counsel against the Most High's "hidden ones" and say, "Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance," which is the stealing of the heritage.
precepts.point: To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Now the stolen side. “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones. They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.”

Wicked nations took crafty counsel to cut Israel off from being a nation and to wipe out the very name of Israel, so that the people became the hidden ones. That is the stealing of the heritage: the identity was robbed and hidden. Restitution restores what was stolen to its proper owner, and the ones it was stolen from are the hidden ones, our people.

precepts.text: "The robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision," meaning the robbers exalt themselves as the Israelites and set up the false claim.
precepts.point: Now the stolen side: wicked nations robbed the heritage, hid the identity, and Edom exalted himself to claim it. That is why the ones calling themselves Jews today are called the synagogue of Satan, because they are not the people of the promise, they are the robbers who established the vision that they are Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Who did the stealing? Daniel says “the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision; but they shall fall.” The robbers of Israel exalt themselves as the Israelites and set up the false claim; that is Edom exalting himself to claim the heritage.

They established the vision that they are Israel, but they shall fall. Restitution means the stolen name and heritage come back to the people they were robbed from.

precepts.text: The Most High knows "the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan," so those who claim to be Jews and are not are the synagogue of Satan.
precepts.point: Now the stolen side: wicked nations robbed the heritage, hid the identity, and Edom exalted himself to claim it. That is why the ones calling themselves Jews today are called the synagogue of Satan, because they are not the people of the promise, they are the robbers who established the vision that they are Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Christ knows the robbers: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

Those who claim to be Jews and are not are the synagogue of Satan. That is why the ones calling themselves Jews today are called that: they are not the people of the promise, they are the robbers who exalted themselves and established the vision that they are Israel. The restitution of all things takes the heritage back from them and restores it to its owners.

precepts.text: The gentiles are named as the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites, the same nations that did the stealing and hiding.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The gentiles are named: “the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.”

These are the nations that did the stealing and the hiding, the Edomites among them. To be part of the restitution you have to have lost something or had something stolen, and the scriptures show the opposite of these nations: they are the ones who robbed. So they are not gentiles being restored or grafted in; the restitution is for Israel.

precepts.text: "The kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force," and the violent were Esau ruling through Rome, who stole it by force.
precepts.point: The kingdom itself was taken by force, and Israel was led away captive into all nations, showing again that our people are the ones who lost it and must have it restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The kingdom itself was stolen: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.”

The violent were Esau ruling through Rome. They took the kingdom by force, and what is taken by force has to be restored to its proper owner. That is the restitution: the kingdom restored again to Israel.

precepts.text: The Comforter, the Holy Ghost, will teach all things and bring all things to remembrance, which is why we are reliving the restitution now.
precepts.point: The kingdom itself was taken by force, and Israel was led away captive into all nations, showing again that our people are the ones who lost it and must have it restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The remembrance of Israel was made to cease, and Christ said how it comes back: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

The Comforter teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance. That is why we are reliving the restitution now, before Christ comes: the remembrance that was lost is being brought back to our people through the Holy Ghost.

precepts.text: Israel would fall by the edge of the sword and be led away captive into all nations, and Jerusalem would be trodden down of the gentiles until the times of the gentiles be fulfilled.
precepts.point: The kingdom itself was taken by force, and Israel was led away captive into all nations, showing again that our people are the ones who lost it and must have it restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Christ told what would happen to the kingdom: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

Israel fell by the sword and was led captive into all nations, and Jerusalem was trodden down of the gentiles. That shows again that our people are the ones who lost the kingdom and the land and must have them restored. And the times of the gentiles being fulfilled is not their salvation; it is their judgment, when the Most High breaks the nations in his land.

precepts.text: "I will break the Assyrian in my land," breaking the nations that seized the land, which is the fulfillment of the times of the gentiles.
precepts.point: The times of the gentiles being fulfilled is not their salvation but their judgment: the Most High breaks the nations in his land. If salvation only means being saved to enslave us, that is not salvation, and it makes no sense that Christ would save the same gentile nations he prophesied would enslave Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
What fulfilling the times of the gentiles looks like: “That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders.”

The Most High breaks the nations in his land. The nations that seized the land are broken and trodden under foot, and their yoke departs from Israel. That is the fulfillment of the times of the gentiles: their judgment, and Israel's restitution.

precepts.text: "Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina," showing two gentile nations in the land, both marked for destruction, not salvation.
precepts.point: The times of the gentiles being fulfilled is not their salvation but their judgment: the Most High breaks the nations in his land. If salvation only means being saved to enslave us, that is not salvation, and it makes no sense that Christ would save the same gentile nations he prophesied would enslave Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent’s root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent.”

Two gentile nations in the land, the Assyrian and Palestina, and both are marked for destruction, not salvation. If salvation only means being saved to enslave us, that is not salvation. It makes no sense that Christ would save the same gentile nations he prophesied would enslave Israel.

precepts.text: The Most High gathers all nations to the valley of Jehoshaphat and pleads with them there, because they scattered his people and parted his land, so the nations are brought down for judgment.
precepts.point: The times of the gentiles being fulfilled is not their salvation but their judgment: the Most High breaks the nations in his land. If salvation only means being saved to enslave us, that is not salvation, and it makes no sense that Christ would save the same gentile nations he prophesied would enslave Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.”

The nations are brought down for judgment, because they scattered his people and parted his land. Israel is his heritage; the nations are the ones who scattered them. So the fulfilling of the times of the gentiles is their judgment, and the restitution of all things is Israel's heritage and land given back.

precepts.text: Blessed be the Most High of Israel, who redeemed his people and raised up salvation to save us from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us, performing the mercy promised to our fathers by the oath sworn to Abraham.
precepts.point: The restitution is tied to the oath and promise, which is us being saved from our enemies and restored to our kingdom and land, because the promise was made to Abraham our father and passed through the royal seed.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Zacharias uses Peter's own words: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began”.

And what those prophets spoke: “That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”.

The restitution is tied to the oath and the promise. It is us being saved from our enemies and from all that hate us, and restored to our kingdom and land, because the promise was made to Abraham our father and passed through the royal seed.

precepts.text: The oath passed to Isaac's seed, "unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries," showing the promise ran through a royal lineage, not through all nations.
precepts.point: The restitution is tied to the oath and promise, which is us being saved from our enemies and restored to our kingdom and land, because the promise was made to Abraham our father and passed through the royal seed.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The oath sworn to Abraham passed to Isaac: “Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father”.

The promise ran through a royal lineage, from Abraham to Isaac to his seed, not through all nations. The countries were given to that seed, and the restitution of all things is that seed, Israel, having them restored.

precepts.text: The Most High made a covenant with Abram, "Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates," so the restitution restores the land of Israel to its proper owners.
precepts.point: The restitution is tied to the oath and promise, which is us being saved from our enemies and restored to our kingdom and land, because the promise was made to Abraham our father and passed through the royal seed.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates”.

The land was given by covenant to Abraham's seed, with its borders named. Restitution restores something lost or stolen to its proper owner, and the proper owners of the land of Israel are Abraham's seed. The restitution of all things restores the land of Israel to them.

precepts.text: "I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth," the passage Peter quotes.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
This is the passage Peter is quoting: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.”

Peter is quoting Moses. Every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

The prophet is raised up from among their brethren, meaning from among men. That proves Christ came through the seed of a man, not immaculate conception. And the Most High put his words in his mouth, which is why every soul that will not hear that prophet is destroyed from among the people.

precepts.text: Aaron married Elisheba and she bore him children, establishing Amminadab in the lineage, because the prophet comes from among the brethren, meaning from a man.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The prophet comes from among the brethren, from a man, so follow the men. “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Here Amminadab and Naashon are established in the lineage of Israel in the days of Moses. Those same names show up in the generation of Christ, which is how we know he was raised up from among his brethren.

precepts.text: "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham," the genealogy tracing the seed of man.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.” Christ has a generation, a genealogy tracing the seed of man, from Abraham through David.

A prophet raised up from among their brethren has to come through the brethren, and this book of his generation is the proof of it.

precepts.text: Aram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Naashon, showing the generation of Christ runs through the lineage of men, the same Amminadab of Exodus 6.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“And Aram begat Aminadab; and Aminadab begat Naasson; and Naasson begat Salmon”. That is the same Amminadab of Exodus 6, whose daughter Aaron married, and the same Naashon.

The generation of Christ runs through the lineage of men, the brethren of Israel that Moses knew. He was raised up from among their brethren, exactly as Moses said.

precepts.text: Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born, because the man carries the seed the way an apple seed determines the tree, not the soil; the man determines the nationality, not the woman.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The generation ends here: “And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.”

The man carries the seed, the way an apple seed determines the tree, not the soil. The man determines the nationality, not the woman. That is why the genealogy is traced through Joseph, and why the prophet raised up from among the brethren came through the seed of a man.

precepts.text: Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, but "there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face," so the prophet like Moses is not Joshua.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Some would say the prophet like Moses was Joshua: “And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.”

But read on, and there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, but he was not that prophet. The prophet like unto Moses was still to come.

precepts.text: A voice out of the cloud says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him," showing Christ is the only other prophet the Most High dealt with face to face and put his words in his mouth.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.”

Hear ye him: the same words Moses used, him shall ye hear in all things. Christ is the only other prophet the Most High dealt with face to face and put his words in his mouth.

Like unto Moses means the same similarities. Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land. Christ is that prophet.

precepts.text: The Most High would set up David's seed that proceeds out of his bowels and establish the throne of his kingdom forever, which is Christ's everlasting kingdom.
precepts.point: "Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The promise to David: “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”

The seed proceeds out of David's bowels, from the body of a man, and the throne of his kingdom is established for ever. That is Christ's everlasting kingdom, and it confirms that the prophet raised up from among the brethren came through the seed of man, David's seed.

precepts.text: The promises were made "to Abraham and his seed... not... to seeds, as of many; but as of one... which is Christ," so the blessing comes through the one seed, Christ, to the same people.
precepts.point: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.”

The promises were made to Abraham and his seed, and the seed through which the blessing comes is one, Christ. The blessing to the kindreds of the earth comes through that one seed to the same people, the children of the covenant Peter is speaking to.

precepts.text: The Most High speaks against "the whole family which I brought up," saying, "You only have I known of all the families of the earth," so "all the kindreds" points to the one family, Israel.
precepts.point: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Kindreds means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor. “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”.

Israel is the whole family brought up out of Egypt, and the Most High says you only have I known of all the families of the earth. So all the kindreds of the earth points to the one family, Israel, that descends from Abraham, not to all nations.

precepts.text: "Thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth... and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed," part of the promise to Abraham through Israel.
precepts.point: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The promise to Abraham passed to Jacob: “And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.”

Jacob's seed would spread abroad in every direction, and in that seed all the families of the earth are blessed. The promise runs through Israel, the family of Abraham spread abroad, which is who Peter calls the children of the covenant.

precepts.text: Israel would be smitten before their enemies and "removed into all the kingdoms of the earth," the same scattered families of the earth that are to be blessed.
precepts.point: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
How did the family spread abroad to the west, east, north and south? “The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.”

Israel was removed into all the kingdoms of the earth. Those are the scattered families of the earth that are to be blessed in Abraham's seed: the one kindred, dispersed everywhere, not every nation.

precepts.text: "The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first," showing the order in which the tribes are redeemed.

The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, the "Jews," and the "Jew and Gentile" and "Jew and Greek" language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes; the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved.

Unto you first means unto Judah, the Jews first. “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

There was an order and a prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin and Levi, the Jews, and Peter is preaching to them.

precepts.text: James writes "to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad," so all twelve tribes are still in view, not three tribes only.

precepts.text: "Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins," and his people are Israel, whom he turns from their iniquities.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: All the people see him walking and praising the Most High, know he is the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful gate, and are filled with wonder, running together to Peter and John at the porch called Solomon's. note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

The healing was not by Peter's own power or holiness. He was not God for doing the work, any more than Elijah was God for raising the dead; it was done by the power of the Most High. This is why the book of Acts is so important, because if you get well versed in Acts you can spiritually kill the white supremacist doctrine and the wicked Christian mindset that has been planted in our people's minds.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: Peter names "the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers," who glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up and denied before Pilate when Pilate was determined to let him go. The oath and promise passed through a royal lineage: Abraham had Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, but Ishmael was rejected and Isaac was chosen.
If the covenant were for all nations, it would have passed through Ishmael too, but it went straight down to Isaac, showing this is not the God of all nations but the God of our fathers.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: They denied the Holy One and the Just and desired a murderer to be granted to them, and killed the Prince of life, whom the Most High raised from the dead, of which the apostles are witnesses. note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: It is his name, through faith in his name, that made this man strong, and the faith which is by him gave the man this perfect soundness in the presence of them all. The strength did not come from the men but from faith in the name of Christ.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: Peter says, "And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it, as did also your rulers," but the things the Most High showed before by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he has so fulfilled. note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord." People say they repented without understanding the scriptural meaning of the words. To repent is to turn from all your transgressions, and to be converted is to change, which requires the law to change to.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you." The "you" is Israel, which was established back in verse 12, so you have to read the whole chapter as one audience being addressed.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began." Restitution is the restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner, the same word used when land seized from our people is demanded back. We are living the restitution of all things right now, before Christ comes.

To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored.

Now the stolen side: wicked nations robbed the heritage, hid the identity, and Edom exalted himself to claim it. That is why the ones calling themselves Jews today are called the synagogue of Satan, because they are not the people of the promise, they are the robbers who established the vision that they are Israel.
The kingdom itself was taken by force, and Israel was led away captive into all nations, showing again that our people are the ones who lost it and must have it restored.

The times of the gentiles being fulfilled is not their salvation but their judgment: the Most High breaks the nations in his land. If salvation only means being saved to enslave us, that is not salvation, and it makes no sense that Christ would save the same gentile nations he prophesied would enslave Israel.

The restitution is tied to the oath and promise, which is us being saved from our enemies and restored to our kingdom and land, because the promise was made to Abraham our father and passed through the royal seed.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things," and every soul that will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people. The prophet is raised up "from among their brethren," meaning from among men, which proves Christ came through the seed of a man, not immaculate conception.

"Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days." All the prophets from Samuel onward foretold these days, tying back to the "you" who are the men of Israel established in verse 12.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities." "Unto you first" means unto Judah, the Jews first, and the "you" being turned from iniquities is Israel, the same audience throughout the chapter.

There was an order and prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, the "Jews," and the "Jew and Gentile" and "Jew and Greek" language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes; the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved.
